description: XCTL site three - the transfer to the card update program, whose verb stands at :566 with PROGRAM(CCARD-NEXT-PROG) at :567. This is the second of the two field-shaped transfers and the one arm of the dispatcher that no other case in this folder reaches. ENTER with 'U' in CRDSEL7I is the only select character on the screen, so 2250-EDIT-ARRAY [:1073-1119] finds exactly one: its INSPECT TALLYING at :1079-1082 counts one - the tally names ALL 'S' and ALL 'U' together, so a 'U' is counted by the same statement an 'S' would be - :1084 IF I > +1 is false and WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION is never set. :1097 zeroes I-SELECTED and the PERFORM VARYING at :1099-1115 walks all seven subscripts: rows one to six take WHEN SELECT-BLANK(I) at :1106 and CONTINUE, because an item the terminal never transmitted arrives as LOW-VALUES and :80-82 names LOW-VALUES a SELECT-BLANK value alongside a space, and row seven takes WHEN SELECT-OK(I) at :1101 - the 88 at :77 names 'S' and 'U' together - where :1102 moves 7 into I-SELECTED. Reaching the arm is itself the assertion this case makes. The EVALUATE TRUE at :418 offers eight arms ahead of it and two of them are live candidates that must be refused for two different reasons. The re-entry arm at :459-460 pairs CDEMO-PGM-REENTER with CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM NOT EQUAL LIT-THISPGM, and although this request does arrive REENTER the commarea names 'COCRDLIC', so the second half fails and the REENTER context passes through untouched. The card-detail arm at :517-519 then tests VIEW-REQUESTED-ON(I-SELECTED) against the very subscript :1102 has just set, and the byte there is 'U' and not 'S', so that arm falls through as well. Only at :545-547 does UPDATE-REQUESTED-ON(I-SELECTED) match. Arm order alone decides which of the two field-shaped transfers fires, and it is decided on one byte. The arm loads CCARD-NEXT-PROG, -MAPSET and -MAP at :554-557 from the LIT-CARDUPD* literal block at :203-210 - LIT-CARDUPDPGM 'COCRDUPC' PIC X(8) [:203-204], LIT-CARDUPDMAPSET 'COCRDUP' PIC X(7) [:207-208] and LIT-CARDUPDMAP 'CCRDUPA' PIC X(7) [:209-210], whose widths are exactly the CCARD-NEXT-PROG X(8), CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET X(7) and CCARD-NEXT-MAP X(7) that app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy declares; LIT-CARDUPDTRANID 'CCUP' PIC X(4) [:205-206] is declared beside them and this arm never moves it, which is preserved by asserting no CDEMO-TO-TRANID. :559-562 hands the selected row's identifiers over in the communication area, read from WS-SCREEN-DATA at the 1-based subscript I-SELECTED, and they are fixture row seven's own bytes: CARD-ACCT-ID at 17-27 and CARD-NUM at 1-16 of a 150-byte CVACT02Y record. Both had just been zeroed - 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT MOVEs ZEROES TO CDEMO-ACCT-ID at :1011 and 2220-EDIT-CARD MOVEs ZEROES TO CDEMO-CARD-NUM at :1046 on the not-supplied path both blank filters take - so the values that travel are the row's and the order of the two effects is part of what is pinned. This case is deliberately the A/B twin of case14. Same seeded fifty rows, same page one, same subscript seven, same outbound 160-byte commarea; the only differences anywhere in the two files are the select character and the three navigation literals it selects. Holding everything else identical is what makes the pair a proof: a diff can only be the dispatcher choosing a different arm. case13 pins the sibling detail arm at subscript 1 and case14 at subscript 7, so between the three the 1-based-to-0-based conversion is asserted at both ends of the OCCURS 7 table [:74-76] on both select characters. The arm performs neither 1000-SEND-MAP nor 9000-READ-FORWARD, so no map is sent, no browse is issued, no FILE STATUS outcome is contributed and the card master is left exactly as it was found - which is what the fifty unchanged expectedFinalState images assert. What comes back is a name plus the commarea the transfer would have passed in COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and the 58-byte WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA cursor [:229-248]; the client resolves the target and no state is held on the server. Five divergences are recorded rather than corrected. First, and the one that changes what this file says: the folder brief states that SET CDEMO-USRTYP-USER and SET CDEMO-PGM-ENTER are present on this arm and absent from the 'S' arm, and the source says otherwise. :520-525 and :548-553 are the same six statements in the same order, SETs included, and CardListController.transferToCard is one method shared by both arms whose comments cite ':522 / :550' and ':523 / :551' for that very pair. The two arms are symmetric apart from the guard and the three literals. The values this case asserts are unchanged - CDEMO-USER-TYPE 'U' and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 0, because :550-551 do set them - but they are not distinguishing marks of this arm and case14 carries them too. Second, the brief's line citations inside the arm run one high throughout, giving :549-563 for statements that stand at :548-562; its :566 for the XCTL verb is right. Third, the three EXEC CICS XCTL verbs stand at :402, :538 and :566 and it is their PROGRAM(...) operands that fall on :403, :539 and :567. Fourth, CVCRD01Y declares 16 CCARD-AID conditions - ENTER, CLEAR, 'PA1  ' and 'PA2  ' space-padded to five, and PFK01 through PFK12, with no PA3 - where the brief says 15; the copybook is authoritative. Fifth, about the folder rather than the source: the brief calls the literal-transfer case case16, which is really the card-filter rejection - the literal PROGRAM(LIT-MENUPGM) transfer is case11 - and this slot previously held a second copy of case12's non-numeric account-filter rejection, so the arm at :545-569 had no declarative case at all and was proven only by COCRDLICParityTest's targeted three-transfer-sites assertion, which drives it at subscript 1. COCRDLIC cannot project the map it names. The COPY list at :221-290 draws in CVCRD01Y, COCOM01Y, DFHBMSCA, DFHAID, COTTL01Y, COCRDLI, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CSUSR01Y and CVACT02Y, with COCRDSL at :274 and CSMSG02Y at :283 commented out - the asterisk sits in column 7 - and no COPY COCRDUP anywhere, so the update map is not in this compile unit in any form; the only trace of it is the mapset name itself, held as the PIC X(7) literal at :208. The program has exactly one SEND MAP [:939] and one RECEIVE MAP [:963], both on CCRDLIA of COCRDLI, so no 17-field COCRDUP projection and no 15-field COCRDSL projection is asserted here: the update mapset enters this program as a name to transfer to and as nothing else, which is what the stateless navigation contract asks of it. Every value here is statically derived - from the program text, from app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy, app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy and app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, from the symbolic map app/cpy-bms/COCRDLI.CPY, and from the real fifty-row app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt - and none of it was captured from a live COBOL run, which this environment cannot perform. The clock is pinned to case01's instant so CURDATEO and CURTIMEO are reproducible, the page stays the behavioural seven of WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES [:177-178] rather than anything configurable, nothing on this path fails edit so no CSSETATY DFHRED-plus-asterisk highlight applies, and COCRDLIC contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' and moves nothing into RETURN-CODE, so the expected return code is zero even though control transfers away.
